scope: Completed E00,D02,D03 execution and negative-result reporting only. E01 matched entity-value treatment justified; no replacement or reliability claim.
review_text:
**APPROVE — completed E00, D02 and D03 execution and negative-result reporting.** I found no blocking leakage, scoring, checkpoint-selection or saved-inference defect. E00 does not justify replacing P05. The matched E01 treatment remains a justified next experiment.

I read the [parent history](<t3-thread://v2/7309f52a-c52b-4287-b6af-6acae8ea63d1/e95afacb-03d8-47cb-bc19-800db47bbdac>) and prior review records. I independently reproduced both saved metric summaries and **all eight development prediction arrays from E00’s selected checkpoint**, verified relevant source/dependency/artifact hashes, and reran the five entity tests successfully. No files, fits, optimizer steps or reserved contents were changed or opened.

**The largest mistakes and remaining weaknesses are these:**

1. **Ward discrimination has deteriorated substantially, despite passing its narrow guards.** False ward predictions increased **282 → 362**; **322 recorded recalls became wards**. Ward type precision is **9.95%**, and complete-command precision is only **1.74%**. Five additional correct ward classifications produced **zero additional correct ward commands**.

   The [guard implementation](F:/Code/battlecode-26-27/tools/action_predictor/entity_analysis.py:28) checks minimum ward successes but imposes no false-positive ceiling. Passing that guard cannot establish acceptable ward behaviour. Preserve the current criteria for this pair; strengthen future experiment criteria prospectively.

2. **Retraining has redistributed successes without improving complete-command accuracy.** E00 gets **11,461/14,439**, versus P05’s **11,472**. Macro F1 falls **0.63239 → 0.62910**. Observed joint NLL improves only **0.66%**, with the paired interval spanning zero benefit. The 11-command difference is not convincing evidence of statistical harm, but it fails the predefined no-regression gate.

   Every category remains accounted for:

   | Category | E00 exact joint | Change in correct commands vs P05 |
   |---|---:|---:|
   | altar | 0/2 — 0% | 0 |
   | attack | 894/985 — 90.76% | +20 |
   | blocked | 7/110 — 6.36% | +6 |
   | cancel | 2,549/2,589 — 98.46% | +14 |
   | cast_0 | 163/213 — 76.53% | +9 |
   | cast_1 | 94/243 — 38.68% | −1 |
   | end | 3,924/4,096 — 95.80% | −33 |
   | move | 1,282/2,362 — 54.28% | −5 |
   | priority | 70/576 — 12.15% | −1 |
   | recall | 2,450/3,084 — 79.44% | −22 |
   | shop | 0/43 — unassessed arguments | 0 |
   | submit | 21/22 — 95.45% | +2 |
   | teleport | 0/2 — 0% | 0 |
   | ward | 7/112 — 6.25% | 0 |

   The exact failure decomposition reproduces: **1,629 wrong types + 1,306 wrong parameters after correct types + 43 unassessed shops = 2,978 failures**. Movement, recall and priority contribute **2,220 failures: 74.5%**.

3. **The model has both fitting and generalization problems.** Falling training objective alongside worsening late development loss supports overfitting. Yet direction-change movement remains weak even on training data. More regularization alone will not resolve the representation, objective or specialization problem.

   Similarly, priority values are exact on only **25.16% of training rows**, and ward joint accuracy is only **8.41% on training**. These failures cannot all be attributed to development distribution shift.

   Comparing overall training accuracy with development accuracy is misleading because augmented training has different category frequencies and many more unassessed shops. The reports correctly acknowledge that limitation.

4. **The frozen argument paths impose strict limits on this experiment.** Even perfect action classification would leave current development parameter ceilings around **60.08% for cast_1**, **21.43% for ward**, and **18.92% for priority**. E01 can improve their action decisions, but cannot repair those argument distributions.

   This is reasonable protection for an isolated entity-input experiment. It cannot remain the permanent architecture if the objective is 90% per category.

5. **The planned E01 reporting currently omits its essential matched comparison.** The [runner](F:/Code/battlecode-26-27/tools/action_predictor/entity_experiment.py:181) produces paired comparisons against M01 and P05; it does not produce **E01 minus E00**. That contrast must be added to E01’s analysis, including category counts, movement contexts and paired group uncertainty. It can be done without changing the frozen fitting source.

   Beating P05 alone would not isolate entity information: E00 already bundles retraining, separate fusions and common priority channels.

6. **Some verification and capacity claims need precise interpretation.**
   
   - The recorded roundtrip’s zero probability error compares identical reconstructed inputs through the same predictor. It establishes input/routing parity; it is not independently a full saved-probability reproduction. My checkpoint reproduction supplies the stronger saved-array check. Six additional single-row versus batch action-probability probes differed by at most **2.24×10⁻⁷**, consistent with floating-point execution differences.
   - **233,566 trainable parameters is a nominal count.** Zeroing entity values leaves some input-dependent weights inactive in E00. Matching shapes and dense computation does not mean matching effective information or active capacity.
   - The complete model contains **545,800 parameters**, including frozen components. Future comparisons should report measured serving latency and memory alongside fit time.
   - The [entity encoding](F:/Code/battlecode-26-27/tools/action_predictor/entity_set.py:23) retains every selected entity, but still compresses buffs into summaries. It is richer entity evidence, rather than a lossless representation of every observable field.

**The diagnostic conclusions are mostly appropriately restrained.** D02’s negative change/continuation gradient cosine supports testing specialization; it does not prove broad multitask interference. D03 does not establish terrain as the cause of movement failures. Nominal weighted ward sample mass is not measured gradient contribution. Encoded-input collisions do not prove inherent randomness or unobservability.

The historical process also spent excessive effort repeating unchanged full-data verification and extending frozen-classifier priority studies. The latest direction correctly changes that allocation. There is no reason to repeat the old 495-game extraction gate or request another routine pre-fit review here.

**Proceed next with the single matched E01 treatment**, using the identical E00 fit source, initialization procedure, rows, normalization, sampler, losses, optimizer settings and checkpoint rule. Change only access to actual entity values. The control’s missed seed gate does not answer whether those values help, so it does not invalidate completing the pair.

For E01’s completed analysis:

- Measure **E01−E00** as well as comparisons with M01/P05.
- Explicitly expose recall→ward errors, ward false positives, movement classification and continuation losses.
- Check the changed entity-value path, padding/permutation behaviour and saved inference; reuse valid immutable evidence.
- Apply the existing repeat gate unchanged. Do not select a later checkpoint for better accuracy.

**After that pair, the strongest substantial alternative is a change-specialized movement model with a causal learned gate.** It directly addresses the largest failure category and the measured local gradient conflict. Use recorded change labels only for supervision and evaluation; inference must predict the gate from available evidence. Judge the complete mixture on joint movement, continuation preservation and all-category regressions.

The next classifier study should compare natural-frequency training and augmentation/weight correction, because recall→ward confusion remains a major source of avoidable failures. Preserve rare recall and ward performance rather than suppressing wards. A fresh GRU versus causal-transformer comparison remains worthwhile with identical observation histories, heads and comparable budgets. Nonlinear priority prediction is also justified later: P05’s conditional mapping is still linear over its supplied features.

The original targets remain unmet: macro F1 is below **0.65**, movement gains only **4.66 points** over the fixed simple baseline, and loss is not 10% below P05 or the strongest simple reference. Attack’s single-seed point estimate above 90%, submit’s 22 examples, and the reused unseen-priority success establish no certification. All 43 shop arguments remain unassessed strict failures; altar and teleport remain uncertified. Five repeatedly reused development groups and one warm-start seed cannot establish untouched generalization or three-seed reliability.

**Retain P05/M01. Complete the controlled entity comparison, then allocate further fitting to the measured failure categories.**
